newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Independent Belgrade radio gets frequency.
newsitem.headline: Independent Belgrade radio gets frequency.

text.p: Independent Belgrade B92 radio, switched off by the government for two days last week, said on Thursday it had signed a new 10-year contract with Radio and Television Serbia which allows it to broadcast via a state-owned transmitter.
It said the contract, which can be automatically extended, was signed by Radio and Television Serbia Director General Dragoljub Milanovic and B92 Radio Director Sasa Mirkovic.
"All doubts about the lawfulness of B92 Radio have thus been removed," the radio said. "This is a success for B92 Radio and it represents a seal of approval for our work so far."
The radio said it would continue to make efforts to obtain its own frequencies.
The authorities switched the radio off last week for two days at the height of massive anti-government demonstrations across Serbia.
B92 was the only electronic media in Serbia which extensively covered the demonstrations.
In Belgrade alone, up to 150,000 people a day protested against fraud at local elections last November.
The opposition claims the ruling socialists of Serbia's President Slobodan Milosevic stole its victory in Belgrade and several other big Serbian cities.
After pressure from the United States and other Western countries, B92 was allowed to resume broadcasting.
